Latin word

dīripiō

dīripiō, dīripere, dīripuī, dīreptum

verb, third conjugation

tear apart; of an enemy’s land or goods, lay waste, plunder, sack

In this lexicon

  • plunder

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 7.8.4: ab hostibus dīripī (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 2.17.2: impedīmentīs dīreptīs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • impedīmentīs dīreptīs

    the baggage having been plunderedCaes. BG 2.17.2 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for plunder

  • quī puerīs in epilogum prōductīs tālōs jēcit in medium, quōs illī dīripere coepērunt

    who, when the children had been brought on for the peroration, threw knucklebones into the middle, and they began to scramble for themQuint. 6.1.47

    In the entry for plunder

  • vāstātī agrī sunt

    the fields were laid wasteLiv. 3.32.2 (Lewis & Short)
